source.snippet: Should HN add the ability to flag articles as AI-generated? This doesn't have to act as a regular flag, i.e., it won't de-rank the article; it could just show up as an indicator, allowing others (like myself) who don't like reading AI-generated text, to skip it. Open questions: 1. Why is the regular voting system not enough? 2. Should HN change in response to the gen AI era? It has been successful not changing fundamentals. [365 points, 194 comments — broad community engagement indicating widespread frustration with undisclosed AI-generated content across the web]

problem_statement: Content curators, newsletter editors, and platform operators cannot reliably identify and label AI-generated articles at scale, causing reader trust erosion and wasted review time when AI content is not disclosed.
target_segment: Newsletter editors, content platform operators, media publishers, and community moderators who curate or gate-keep content feeds and need to flag or filter AI-generated submissions.
notes: 365 upvotes and 194 comments on HN is a strong community signal. The discussion implies platform operators and editors want tooling — not just personal readers. Potential paying buyers: newsletter platforms, community platforms (forums, aggregators), media companies that want to audit submitted content. Adjacent products (Originality.ai, GPTZero) already charge $10–$30/mo per seat, validating willingness to pay. Buyer signal is indirect but plausible; signal_strength capped at 3 because the thread is a feature request aimed at HN itself, not a direct 'I pay for X and it doesn't do Y' complaint.
